settings.editor: One trusted school for Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody. With the mountains at your back and every local test route covered, BuckleUp's ICBC-certified instructor , Farhad Sanafefar , gets Tri-Cities drivers ready for anything.

The Tri-Cities — Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody — give new drivers a great mix of real BC driving conditions. Students can practise hills around Westwood Plateau and Heritage Mountain, busier roads like Lougheed Highway and Barnet Highway, railway crossings in Port Coquitlam, and busy local areas such as Town Centre and Newport Village.

BuckleUp is based in Port Moody and teaches across the Tri-Cities. Our ICBC-certified instructor ,Farhad, tailors each lesson to your level, whether you are a beginner or preparing for your road test. Lessons may include quiet residential driving, parking, hill starts, lane changes, highway merging, rail crossings, and other key skills needed for safe, confident driving.
From Westwood Plateau and Heritage Mountain hills to PoCo rail crossings and the Lougheed corridor, we train on them all.
Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody — one trusted, local school  across the whole region.
Fully ICBC-certified, led by senior instructor Farhad Sanaeifar.

ICBC Road Test Prep in the Tri-Cities

settings.editor: Test centre: Coquitlam ICBC Driver Licensing office (the main test centre for Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody)

Most Tri-Cities road tests are booked through the Coquitlam ICBC Driver Licensing office, which serves Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody. Because the area includes busy roads, hills, railway crossings, and residential streets, students need well-rounded local practice.

At BuckleUp, we help you prepare by focusing on key skills such as lane changes, hill starts, parking, speed control, intersections, and safe decision-making in real Tri-Cities driving conditions.

icon_list.text: Be equally confident on hills (Westwood Plateau, Heritage Mountain) and on level rail crossings (Port Coquitlam) — Tri-Cities routes mix both.
Practise multi-lane changes and merges on the Lougheed and Barnet Highway corridors.
Rehearse a full range of parking — parallel, stall, and hill — since residential test streets vary across the three cities.
Know the school and pedestrian zones around Town Centre, Newport Village, and Downtown PoCo where speed control is heavily scored.

settings.editor: Common questions about driving lessons in Tri-Cities.

tabs.tab_title: Which cities do you cover in the Tri-Cities?
tabs.tab_content: We provide driving lessons across all three Tri-Cities — Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody — with pickup from home, work, school, or a SkyTrain station anywhere in the region.

tabs.tab_title: Where will I take my Tri-Cities road test?
tabs.tab_content: Most Tri-Cities road tests are booked at the Coquitlam ICBC Driver Licensing office, which serves Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody. We train you on those exact routes regardless of which city you live in.

tabs.tab_title: Do you cover both the hills and the rail crossings?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. The Tri-Cities mix steep grades (Westwood Plateau, Heritage Mountain) with Port Coquitlam's level rail crossings, and our lessons prepare you confidently for both.

tabs.tab_title: How many lessons will I need to pass in the Tri-Cities?
tabs.tab_content: Most beginners need around six to ten lessons. After a free assessment, your instructor will recommend a plan based on the test routes you'll be driving.

tabs.tab_title: Do you offer driving lessons in Farsi across the Tri-Cities?
tabs.tab_content: Yes. Lessons are available in both English and Farsi throughout Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, and Port Moody.
